topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: What is the stated statutory purpose of the South Carolina Real Estate Commission under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-10?
choice_a: To regulate the real estate industry so as to protect the public's interest in real estate transactions
choice_b: To promote membership in local real estate trade associations
choice_c: To set standard commission rates charged by all licensees
choice_d: To administer county property tax assessments
explanation: Section 40-57-10 creates the South Carolina Real Estate Commission and states its purpose is "to regulate the real estate industry so as to protect the public's interest" when the public is involved in real estate transactions.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-10 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: The South Carolina Real Estate Commission operates under the administrative umbrella of which state agency?
choice_a: The Department of Revenue
choice_b: The Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation (LLR)
choice_c: The Secretary of State's office
choice_d: The Department of Consumer Affairs
explanation: Section 40-57-10 places the Commission "under the administration of the Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation," consistent with how LLR houses SCREC and hosts its licensing laws at llr.sc.gov/re.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-10 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: How is the South Carolina Real Estate Commission generally composed under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-40?
choice_a: Five commissioners, all of whom must be licensed brokers-in-charge
choice_b: Fifteen commissioners appointed entirely by the state legislature
choice_c: Ten commissioners, including seven actively practicing real estate professionals (one per congressional district) and two public members appointed by the Governor
choice_d: Three commissioners appointed solely by the Governor with no Senate role
explanation: Section 40-57-40 establishes a ten-member commission made up mostly of licensed real estate professionals elected by congressional district, plus public members appointed by the Governor with Senate advice and consent.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-40 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-40, what is the length of a term served by a member of the South Carolina Real Estate Commission?
choice_a: Two years
choice_b: Six years
choice_c: One year, renewed annually
choice_d: Four years
explanation: Commission members serve four-year terms under Section 40-57-40, with vacancies filled by the same appointment or election method used for the original seat.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-40 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Which of the following is a power or duty the South Carolina Real Estate Commission holds under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-60?
choice_a: Determining qualification standards for licensure, conducting disciplinary hearings, and promulgating regulations
choice_b: Setting the sale price for all listed residential real estate in the state
choice_c: Acting as the exclusive escrow agent for every closing in South Carolina
choice_d: Appointing county tax assessors
explanation: Section 40-57-60 gives the Commission authority to administer and enforce the chapter, set qualification standards, hold disciplinary hearings, recommend legislation, promulgate regulations, set fee schedules, and conduct compliance inspections.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-60 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-20, what is required before a person may act as, or advertise services as, a real estate broker, associate, or property manager in South Carolina?
choice_a: Filing a fictitious business name registration with the Secretary of State
choice_b: Holding an active, valid license issued by the commission
choice_c: Posting a certificate of completion at the licensee's place of business
choice_d: Recording a notice of intent to practice with the county register of deeds
explanation: Section 40-57-20 makes it unlawful to act as, or advertise or provide services as, a real estate broker, associate, or property manager without an active, valid license issued by the commission.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-20 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under the definitions in S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-30, activities such as negotiating the listing, sale, purchase, exchange, or lease of real estate for another generally trigger a licensure requirement when performed:
choice_a: Only when the transaction value exceeds a set dollar threshold
choice_b: Only when the activity is advertised in a newspaper or online listing service
choice_c: For a fee, salary, commission, referral fee, or other valuable consideration
choice_d: Only when performed by someone who resides outside South Carolina
explanation: Section 40-57-30 defines a "broker" (and similarly an "associate") as one who performs brokerage-type activities for a fee, salary, commission, referral fee, or other valuable consideration; compensation for the activity, not transaction size or advertising, is what triggers licensure.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-30 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240, which of the following is exempt from South Carolina real estate licensure requirements?
choice_a: A property management company managing units it does not own, in exchange for a management fee
choice_b: A licensed broker representing a homebuilder in new home sales
choice_c: A person who receives a referral fee for introducing a buyer to a licensed broker
choice_d: An unlicensed owner who sells, leases, or rents real estate in which the owner holds an interest identical to the interest being conveyed
explanation: Section 40-57-240 exempts an unlicensed owner selling, leasing, or renting real estate when the interest being conveyed is identical to the owner's own legal interest in the property; the other options describe activity requiring licensure.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240, an attorney at law is exempt from South Carolina real estate licensure requirements when:
choice_a: Acting within the scope of legal representation of a client or owner
choice_b: Selling any real estate at all, regardless of whether a client relationship exists
choice_c: Advertising general real estate brokerage services to the public
choice_d: Managing rental property as an unrelated side business
explanation: The attorney exemption in Section 40-57-240 is limited to an attorney acting within the scope of duties involved in the legal representation of a client or owner, not general brokerage activity unrelated to legal representation.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240, which category of persons is exempt from licensure when acting within the scope of their official duties?
choice_a: Nonprofit charities disposing of donated real property
choice_b: Agencies and instrumentalities of state or federal government, and their employees
choice_c: Licensed accountants who occasionally assist clients in listing property
choice_d: Auctioneers selling any type of real property
explanation: Section 40-57-240 exempts agencies and instrumentalities of the state or federal government, and their employees, acting within the scope of their official duties.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240, a forester registered under Title 48, Chapter 27 is exempt from real estate licensure when:
choice_a: The forester also holds a general contractor's license
choice_b: The land parcel being sold is smaller than ten acres
choice_c: The sale of any land involved is merely incidental to the sale of timber on that land
choice_d: The forester is selling land on behalf of an immediate family member
explanation: Section 40-57-240 exempts foresters registered under Title 48, Chapter 27 specifically when any land sale is merely incidental to the sale of timber on that land, not for general land sale activity.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240, court-appointed receivers and trustees are exempt from South Carolina real estate licensure requirements when:
choice_a: They have completed sixty hours of commission-approved real estate coursework
choice_b: The property being sold is valued under a set dollar amount
choice_c: They register annually with the commission as an exempt party
choice_d: Acting within the scope of their court appointment
explanation: Section 40-57-240 exempts court-appointed receivers and trustees while they are acting within the scope of their court appointment, without any coursework or annual registration condition.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-240 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110, into which classifications does the South Carolina Real Estate Commission issue individual licenses?
choice_a: Broker, broker-in-charge, and associate
choice_b: Agent, sub-agent, and dual agent
choice_c: Salesperson, appraiser, and home inspector
choice_d: Trainee, journeyman, and master licensee
explanation: Section 40-57-110 provides for issuance and classification of licenses as broker, broker-in-charge, or associate.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110, may an individual hold licenses in more than one classification at the same time, or transfer a license to another person?
choice_a: Yes, as long as both licenses are renewed on the same renewal date
choice_b: No — an individual may not be licensed in more than one classification at the same time, and a license is not transferable
choice_c: Yes, a license may be transferred to an immediate family member
choice_d: Yes, provided the commission grants written approval for dual classification
explanation: Section 40-57-110 states that no individual may be licensed in more than one classification at the same time and that a license is not transferable.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110, what happens when a South Carolina real estate license is placed on inactive status?
choice_a: It automatically becomes void after ninety days on inactive status
choice_b: The licensee may continue to negotiate transactions only for pre-existing clients
choice_c: It may remain inactive indefinitely if properly renewed, but the licensee may not engage in real estate brokerage activity while inactive
choice_d: It automatically converts to broker-in-charge status once reactivated
explanation: Under Section 40-57-110, a licensee may place a license on inactive status indefinitely by notifying the commission and continuing to renew, but an inactive licensee is prohibited from practicing real estate brokerage while inactive.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110, what generally happens to a license that remains lapsed (unrenewed) through the last day of the twenty-fourth month following its expiration date?
choice_a: The license automatically converts to inactive status with no further action needed
choice_b: The licensee is granted an automatic additional twelve-month grace period
choice_c: The license remains valid, but the licensee must retake only the state portion of the exam
choice_d: The license is canceled and generally cannot be reinstated
explanation: Section 40-57-110 provides that a license lapsed through the last day of the twenty-fourth month following expiration is canceled, generally without a path to reinstatement.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-110 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-115, which criminal background checks must initial applicants and license renewal candidates submit to?
choice_a: A SLED state fingerprint-based check, an FBI national fingerprint-based check, and a Social Security number-based records check
choice_b: Only a county-level criminal background check
choice_c: A credit history check performed by the commission
choice_d: No formal background check; only a signed affidavit of good moral character
explanation: Section 40-57-115 requires a SLED state fingerprint-based criminal records check, a national FBI fingerprint-based check, and a Social Security number-based records check from a commission-approved source.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-115 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-115, who is responsible for the cost of the required criminal records checks for licensure?
choice_a: The South Carolina Real Estate Commission
choice_b: The applicant
choice_c: The applicant's sponsoring broker-in-charge
choice_d: The Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation, from general fund appropriations
explanation: Section 40-57-115 states that the costs of conducting the required criminal records checks must be borne by the applicant.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-115 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-120, a South Carolina licensee who changes residency status (becoming a resident or a nonresident) must notify the commission in writing of the change within:
choice_a: Ten days
choice_b: Ninety days
choice_c: Thirty days
choice_d: One year, at the next renewal cycle
explanation: Section 40-57-120 requires a licensee to notify the commission in writing within thirty days of a change in residency status; failure to comply can subject the licensee to disciplinary action.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-120 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-310, what is the minimum age to apply for licensure as a South Carolina real estate broker or broker-in-charge?
choice_a: Eighteen years old
choice_b: Twenty-five years old
choice_c: There is no minimum age requirement
choice_d: Twenty-one years old
explanation: Section 40-57-310 requires an applicant for licensure as a broker or broker-in-charge to have attained the age of twenty-one.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-310 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-310, what is the minimum age to apply for licensure as a South Carolina real estate associate?
choice_a: Eighteen years old
choice_b: Twenty-one years old
choice_c: Sixteen years old
choice_d: There is no minimum age requirement
explanation: Section 40-57-310 sets the minimum age to apply for an associate license at eighteen, lower than the age-twenty-one requirement for broker or broker-in-charge applicants.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-310 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320, what pre-licensing classroom education is generally required of an applicant for a South Carolina real estate associate license?
choice_a: A single thirty-hour introductory course with no advanced component
choice_b: Sixty hours of instruction in fundamentals of real estate principles and practices, plus thirty hours of advanced real estate principles instruction
choice_c: A four-year college degree in real estate or business administration
choice_d: One hundred twenty hours of continuing education completed after initial licensure
explanation: Section 40-57-320 requires completion of sixty hours of classroom instruction in fundamentals of real estate principles and practices and thirty hours of advanced real estate principles instruction within five years before applying, for an associate license.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320, in addition to classroom instruction, what active experience requirement generally applies to an applicant seeking a South Carolina broker license?
choice_a: Two years of any real estate-related employment, licensed or not
choice_b: No experience requirement beyond passing the examination
choice_c: Five years of active associate licensure within the past seven years
choice_d: Ten years of licensure in any U.S. state
explanation: Section 40-57-320 requires a broker applicant to have completed commission-approved classroom instruction and to have held active associate licensure for five years within the preceding seven years.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320, once approved to sit for the required South Carolina license examination, how long does an applicant generally have to successfully complete all portions of the exam?
choice_a: Thirty days
choice_b: Six months
choice_c: An indefinite period, with no deadline
choice_d: A twelve-month eligibility period
explanation: Section 40-57-320 gives an examination candidate a twelve-month eligibility period in which to successfully complete all portions of the examination.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320, an applicant who passes all required portions of the license examination must apply for licensure within what time frame, or be required to reapply and retake the entire examination?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Thirty days
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: There is no deadline to apply after passing
explanation: Section 40-57-320 requires an applicant who has passed the examination to apply for a license within one year, or reapply and retake all portions of the examination.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-320 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-330, an individual holding an active broker or associate license in South Carolina must:
choice_a: Operate entirely independently, with no broker-in-charge affiliation required
choice_b: Be licensed under a broker-in-charge, and may not be licensed under more than one broker-in-charge at the same time
choice_c: Be licensed simultaneously under at least two broker-in-charges for coverage purposes
choice_d: Register directly with the Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation without any broker-in-charge sponsorship
explanation: Section 40-57-330 requires an individual holding an active broker or associate license to be licensed under a broker-in-charge, and prohibits being licensed under more than one broker-in-charge during the same period.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-330 (Real Estate License Law)

topic: South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements
question: Under S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-345, a South Carolina licensee who is sixty-five years of age or older with twenty-five or more years of licensure in good standing in the state may renew an expired license and additionally becomes:
choice_a: Exempt from all licensing fees for the remainder of their career
choice_b: Automatically elevated to broker-in-charge status
choice_c: Exempt from continuing education requirements
choice_d: Required to retake only the state portion of the examination
explanation: Section 40-57-345 allows a licensee age sixty-five or older with twenty-five or more years of South Carolina licensure in good standing to renew an expired license and become exempt from continuing education requirements.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-57-345 (Real Estate License Law)
